subs.text: Book twenty-one.
Odysseus Strings His Bow.
Scene one.
Penelope Retrieves the Bow.
Athena inspires Penelope to begin the contest that will expose the suitors to slaughter.
The queen enters the storeroom, unlocks the doors, and lifts Odysseus's bow and quiver down.
Athena sits with the weapon across her knees and weeps before carrying it to the hall.
Two maids carry in the chest of iron, and the axes are set down ringing on the floor of the hall.

scenes.title: The Contest Is Set
scenes.card: The queen announces the contest; her son nearly strings the bow himself, until his father signals him to stop.

subs.text: Scene two.
The Contest Is Set.
Hear me, lords.
Here is the great bow of Odysseus.
Whoever strings it with his own hands and sends an arrow clean through all twelve axes,
I will go with that man, and leave this house I came to as a bride.
Eumaeus and Philoetius weep at the sight of their master's weapon.
Take your crying outside, you fools.
You are spoiling her heart.
Telemachus plants the axes in a straight line and tries the bow three times.
On the fourth attempt he nearly strings it, but Odysseus signals him to stop.

scenes.title: The Suitors Fail the Bow
scenes.card: One suitor after another fails to bend the bow, and the shamed suitors postpone the contest.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Suitors Fail the Bow.
I cannot bend it.
Let another try.
But I tell you, this bow will take the life and the breath out of the best men here,
and better to die than live on failing at what we came for.
One after another they took it up, and braced it, and sweated, and set it down again, and the bow did not move.
Melanthius lights a fire and brings fat so the bow can be warmed and greased.
Even Eurymachus cannot string it and suffers humiliation.
Enough.
It is Apollo's day.
Pour the wine, and we finish this tomorrow.

If Odysseus walked through that gate this hour, which side would you two stand on?

The herdsmen embrace him and weep, then swear support.

subs.text: Scene five.
The Beggar Requests the Bow.
To test your strength with the bow?
Then they roared at him, and under the anger ran a colder thing,
that a beggar might do what their hands could not.
Let the stranger have the bow.
He is a guest in my house, and no guest is refused here.
And if he strings it, I will give him a cloak and a tunic, a spear, and a sword,
and send him wherever his heart wants to go.
Your mother upstairs.
Eumaeus carries the bow through the shouting crowd to Odysseus.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Doors Are Secured.
Eurycleia locks the women into their quarters at Telemachus's instruction.
Philoetius fastens the courtyard gate with a ship's cable.
Odysseus turns the bow in his hands, inspecting every part while the suitors mock him.
The doors are shut.
The cable is knotted.
Every way out of that hall is closed, and the men inside it are still laughing.

scenes.card: The beggar strings the bow with ease and shoots an arrow through all twelve axes; his son arms and joins him.

subs.text: Scene seven.
The Bow Sings.
Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.
Hear that.
It still sings.
It is time, son of Laertes.
I have set my sign on the day.
Telemachus places sword and spear beside him and moves to his father's side.
Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.
Tells you that the stranger has not disgraced the house and signals the next phase.
